newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond futures trend higher ahead of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond futures trend higher ahead of GDP.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bond futures extend their recent rally in anticipation of only a moderate outcome in first quarter GDP when data is released on Wednesday.
*RBA unlikely to ease policy, but market to stay jumpy.
Long-dated Australian bond futures extended their recent rally in anticipation of only a moderate outcome in first quarter GDP when data is released on Wednesday.

Forecasts centre on a 0.8 percent rise after the 0.5 percent growth seen in the December quarter, although one local bank is expecting only a 0.25 percent rise, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
However, annual growth would only be 2.2 percent based on median expectations compared with 3.1 percent in the previous quarter as a large rise in the March 1996 quarter is taken out of the equation.
Before the data the market will be on tenterhooks to see if the Reserve Bank has endorsed a further easing in policy following today's monthly board meeting.

While such a move is unlikley so soon after the last cut on May 23, the market is taking nothing for granted given that it was taken totally off-guard by the easing to 5.5 percent, and it will be holding a collective breath at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) when rate changes are normally announced.
Peter Clay, strategist at Citibank Australia does not expect the RBA to ease again prior to the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2.
"While they (the RBA) have a strong preference to ease policy again, any move will be subject to the requirement of maintaining their inflation-fighting credibility," Clay said.

While he expects an easing in the third quarter, offshore developments may make it difficult for the central bank to ease policy, which could result in a length delay, or even cancellation of such a move.

Local turnover was relatively light, although the 10-year bond futures contract struck a 3-1/2 month high at 92.670, while there continued to be a further unwinding of recent spread steepening trades which held back the short-end.
Meanwhile, there was active issuance of non-government debt with three issues confirmed as launched and a fourth expected to be imminent.

The three offerings announced were a A$500 million four tranche securitisation deal for Macquarie Bank's PUMA, a two-year A$300 million issue for St George Bank and a three-year A$200 million offering from BTR Nylex.
Market sources also said that the ANZ Banking Group is close to launching a three-year A$200 million fixed rate issue at a spread of 25 basis points over.

The local market was slightly outperforming the U.S. in early after hours trading, and margins were again tightening to Canada. Spreads had widened to Canada after the Liberal party held power after today's election, although they had narrowed when initial results suggested they might lose.
